_about: One line per table: what it is for, what personal information it holds, and how long it is kept. Read by server/src/scripts/schemaBible.ts, which refuses to write the schema chapter while any table is missing here. 'Not set' marks a retention period the owner has yet to decide (docs/database/13_PLAN.md); it is written as such, never guessed.

orgs.retention: While the organisation is a customer; closure process not set.

members.purpose: Who belongs to an organisation, with their role.
members.personal: Name and work e-mail of recruiters.
members.retention: While the person is a member; a departure is recorded (left_at), deletion period not set.

portal_members.purpose: Who may work in which portal, and when they were last seen.
portal_members.personal: Links a person to a portal; last activity time.

portal_invitations.purpose: Invitations to join a portal and their e-mail delivery state.
portal_invitations.personal: Invitee e-mail; inviter e-mail. The token is kept only as a hash.
portal_invitations.retention: Until accepted, revoked or expired; clean-up period not set.

portal_capacity.purpose: How many upload slots each portal has reserved.

quota_holds.purpose: Short-lived holds on a portal's upload allowance.

org_settings.purpose: Each organisation's current settings (edit policy, limits, matching).
org_settings.retention: While the organisation is a customer.

org_settings_history.purpose: Every version of an organisation's settings, for the audit trail.
org_settings_history.retention: As long as the records those settings governed.

documents.purpose: Each uploaded CV or job description: its processing state and where its original is stored.
documents.personal: File name, uploader, and the extracted text of a CV (source_text): high sensitivity.
documents.retention: Until the organisation deletes it (deletion.ts removes the original, text and record together).

candidates.purpose: The candidate panel built from a CV, with evidence and the recruiter's edits.
candidates.personal: Everything the CV states about the person: high sensitivity.
candidates.retention: Until the organisation deletes it; edit history scrubbed of personal detail on deletion.

jobs.purpose: The job specification built from a job description.
jobs.personal: Normally none; a contact name if the description names one.

matches.purpose: Each match a recruiter asked for, with its evidence, gaps and confidence, frozen at the versions matched.
matches.personal: Derived from the candidate: high sensitivity.
matches.retention: Removed with the candidate or the job.

upload_batches.purpose: Each batch of uploads: what was declared, refused, duplicated and finished.
upload_batches.personal: Who uploaded; file names of duplicates.

batch_acknowledgements.purpose: Who has seen a batch's report.
batch_acknowledgements.personal: Links a person to a batch.

upload_history_removed.purpose: A permanent line for each deleted document: that it existed and who removed it, with no contents.
upload_history_removed.personal: Who uploaded and who deleted (no names of candidates).
upload_history_removed.retention: Permanent by design (it proves deletions happened).

queue.purpose: Durable background jobs (extraction, deletion, model work) with leases and retries.
queue.personal: Job payloads name documents by id only.
queue.retention: Finished jobs: clean-up period not set.

outbox.purpose: Messages to send after a change commits (invitation e-mails), delivered at least once.
outbox.personal: Recipient details inside the payload until sent.
outbox.retention: Until delivered or dead; clean-up period not set.

mail_attempts.purpose: Each attempt to deliver an outbox message.
mail_attempts.personal: Recipient as a hash and its domain only.

mail_suppressions.purpose: Addresses that must not be mailed again (hard bounces, complaints).

audit_events.purpose: Who did what, when, from what to what. Append-only (trigger audit_no_update); personal detail is scrubbed on deletion.
audit_events.retention: As long as the records it describes.

error_register.purpose: The learning register: every corrected or failed extraction, with its cause and evidence.
error_register.personal: Values from documents (from and to): high sensitivity.
error_register.retention: Not set; removed with the document.

error_occurrences.purpose: Each time a known failure happened.

defect_groups.purpose: Failures grouped by cause, with their status.
defect_groups.personal: None beyond who changed the status.

applications.purpose: A candidate's workflow status for one job (shortlisted, not suitable, interviewed, hired): who set it and when; the history is in the audit log.
applications.personal: Links a person to a job decision: medium sensitivity.
applications.retention: Not set; removed with the candidate or the job.

model_reviews.purpose: Each time the local model reviewed a document or a match, with the model and prompt versions.
model_reviews.personal: The model's answer may quote the document: high sensitivity.
model_reviews.retention: Not set; removed with the document.

model_proposals.purpose: Each correction the model proposed and what the recruiter decided.
model_proposals.retention: Not set; removed with the document.

signup_challenges.purpose: Sign-up codes, stored only as hashes, single use.
signup_challenges.retention: Until used or expired; clean-up period not set.

password_resets.purpose: Password-reset codes, stored only as hashes, single use.
password_resets.retention: Until used or expired; clean-up period not set.

signed_out_sessions.purpose: Sessions ended before their tokens expire, so a copied token is refused.
signed_out_sessions.retention: Until the token would have expired.

rate_limits.purpose: Shared counters that limit guessing and floods across servers.
rate_limits.personal: Keys may contain an address or account id.

console_owner.purpose: The console's accounts: two at most, the owner and their father (owner 12 Nov 2026, migration 052; a third row is impossible).
console_owner.personal: Each account's e-mail; the password only as an argon2id hash.
console_owner.retention: While the account exists; removed at the PC's terminal (console-password.sh --remove).

console_sessions.purpose: The owner's console sessions, known only by a hash of their id.
console_sessions.personal: A short browser description (for example 'Mac · Safari') and which console account it belongs to; no address.
console_sessions.retention: Not set; ended sessions are kept for the owner's own list.

owner_events.purpose: Alerts for the owner: what went wrong, how often, and whether it is back to normal.
owner_events.personal: None: written by our own code from counts and states.
owner_events.retention: Not set; the console shows the last 7 days.

ai_usage.purpose: One row per call to Claude (Anthropic, owner 8 Nov 2026): organisation, portal, billing account, purpose, model, tokens (cache reads and writes apart) and cost; what each portal's monthly bill and the platform's safety cap are counted from. Each organisation reads its own lines; each portal only its own.
ai_usage.personal: None: no text of any question or answer, no name or address; only the organisation, portal and account ids.
ai_usage.retention: Kept for 7 years as billing records; a deleted portal's or organisation's rows lose their ids.

ai_platform_month.purpose: The platform's AI spend per Johannesburg month, settled and held, kept by a trigger on ai_usage on every write to it (066_ai_platform_month.sql); every call reserves against it, so the platform's monthly budget is held exactly.
ai_platform_month.personal: None: a month and two sums of money.
ai_platform_month.retention: Kept with the ai_usage rows it sums: 7 years.

console_codes.purpose: The console's second sign-in step (18_CONSOLE_V0.md, slice 2): the code e-mailed to the owner after the right password, bound to the browser that entered it.
console_codes.personal: Which console account it was sent to; otherwise a hash of the browser's pending token and a hash of the code bound to it; no browser or code.
console_codes.retention: Deleted 1 day after it was issued; a code works for 10 minutes, once.

identity_accounts.purpose: Our own sign-in's accounts (20_IDENTITY_V1.md), off until IDENTITY=own: the same ids as today's accounts.
identity_accounts.personal: E-mail address, the name given at sign-up and what the sign-up was for; the password only as an argon2id hash.
identity_accounts.retention: While the person has an account; removed with the account, its sessions and codes going with it.

identity_sessions.purpose: Each signed-in session of our own sign-in: when it began, was last refreshed and ended, and why.
identity_sessions.personal: Which account; no address, browser or token (the refresh token only as a SHA-256 hash).
identity_sessions.retention: An open session ends after 7 days unused or 30 days in all; an ended one is deleted 90 days after it ended (one never signed out counts as ended at its 30-day limit), so a reused token or a sign-out can be looked into for a quarter.

identity_codes.purpose: E-mailed sign-up and password-reset codes of our own sign-in: one live code per account and purpose, used once.
identity_codes.personal: Which account; the code only as a keyed digest.
identity_codes.retention: Deleted 2 days after it was issued, whether used, replaced or expired (a code works for OTP_EXPIRY_MINUTES), as signup_challenges and password_resets.

billing_accounts.purpose: Each organisation's own billing account, opened by the database when the organisation is created (owner 8 Nov 2026: every new organisation comes with an isolated bill). Its id is what AI use is billed to.
billing_accounts.personal: None: an organisation id, the account's own id and when it was opened.
billing_accounts.retention: Kept while the organisation exists; deleted with it (its usage lines keep their figures).

ai_rate.purpose: The platform's shared per-minute count of what has been asked of each Claude model (requests, input and output tokens), so every server together stays inside Anthropic's limits.
ai_rate.personal: None: a model name, a minute and three counts.
ai_rate.retention: A day; the AI worker deletes older minutes every hour.

fx_rates.purpose: The rand per US dollar for each day (the European Central Bank's reference rate), so each company's AI use is shown in rands at the rate of its own day (migration 048).
fx_rates.retention: Kept: a past day's rate explains a past bill.

portal_daily.purpose: Each portal's totals for each day (CVs and jobs read, matches, shortlisted, failed, AI calls and cost), so the owner's console reads a row per portal per day instead of every action (migration 048).
portal_daily.retention: While the portal exists; removed with it.

console_actions.purpose: Every action the owner took in the console (a person signed out, blocked or deleted; a portal or company deleted; an allowance set; support access opened), with what it touched and its counts and reason (migration 050).
console_actions.personal: The name and e-mail of a person acted on, a company's name, and which console account acted (migration 052).
console_actions.retention: For the life of the platform: it is the record of what the owner did. Nothing may change or remove a row.

support_access.purpose: Each time the owner opened a portal's log for support, with the reason and the hour it was open; the company sees it in its own log (migration 050).

file_removals.purpose: Original files of portals and companies the owner deleted, waiting for the monitor to remove them from the vault (migration 050).
file_removals.personal: The file's path in the vault, which names no one.
file_removals.retention: Until the file is gone: each row is removed once its file is.
